task.title: STOCK
task.spec:
You are working in a checkout of shopizer, a Java e-commerce platform (Maven, several modules; JDK 21 is installed and JAVA_HOME is set).

Merchants report that stock levels are wrong. When an order is placed, the stock of the products ordered often doesn't go down, and sometimes another product's stock goes down instead. Cancelling an order never gives the stock back. Shoppers can put more in their cart than we have, and can check out orders we can't fill. A product with no stock left is still shown as available.

Make stock right everywhere it is used. "Stock" is the "quantity" that GET /api/v2/product/{sku} shows for a product.

- Checkout (POST /api/v1/cart/{code}/checkout and POST /api/v1/auth/cart/{code}/checkout) takes exactly the ordered quantity from the stock of each product ordered, and changes no other product's stock.
- If any product in the cart has less stock than the cart's quantity of it, checkout is refused with HTTP 409 Conflict: no order is created, no stock changes, and the cart stays as it was.
- A cart change that would leave the cart holding more of a product than its stock is refused with HTTP 409 Conflict and leaves the cart as it was. This applies to creating a cart (POST /api/v1/cart/), changing one product's quantity (PUT /api/v1/cart/{code}) and changing several at once (POST /api/v1/cart/{code}/multi, where either every change is made or none is). A product with no stock can't be added at all (HTTP 409). Lowering a quantity or removing a product is always allowed.
- Setting an order's status to CANCELED (PUT /api/v1/private/orders/{id}/status) puts each ordered product's quantity back into its stock. This happens once: setting CANCELED again on an order that is already canceled changes nothing. A canceled order can't be given any other status (HTTP 409 Conflict, and stock is unchanged). Other status changes don't change stock.
- GET /api/v2/product/{sku} shows "available": false and "canBePurchased": false for a product with no stock, and shows it as available again once it has stock. A product the merchant marked unavailable stays unavailable whatever its stock.

When you have finished, reply with one short paragraph saying what you changed.

findings.problem: The cart-add path validates only the newly submitted quantity, then increments an existing line without validating the combined quantity.
findings.impact: Repeated POST /api/v1/cart/ additions can leave a cart holding more than available stock, violating the cart quantity limit.
findings.correction: Validate cartItem.getQuantity() plus the existing line quantity before assigning the combined value; reject the operation with InventoryConflictException before mutating or saving the cart.

findings.problem: createCartItem validates every positive requested quantity before modifyCart determines whether the request lowers an existing line. The same validation is repeated at line 932.
findings.impact: If stock falls below a cart's current quantity, a request that lowers the quantity can still be rejected when the new positive quantity remains above current stock, contrary to the requirement that lowering a quantity is always allowed.
findings.correction: For existing lines, compare the requested quantity with the current quantity first; allow decreases and removals without stock validation, and validate only additions or increases against stock.

findings.problem: The PR adds no regression tests for checkout reservation, insufficient-stock rollback, cart atomicity, cancellation restoration/idempotency, canceled-status transitions, or zero-stock product flags.
findings.impact: The required acceptance behaviors are unproven; the reported order test was skipped and GitHub supplied no checks, so material regressions can pass review undetected.
findings.correction: Add executable integration/unit coverage for all listed acceptance paths, including distinct SKUs, failed multi-update preservation, cancellation once-only behavior, and v2 availability flags; run and report those tests successfully.

runs.report:
## Scope and repository confirmation
The requested checkout, cart, order-status, inventory, and v2 product behavior is implemented in this Shopizer checkout (`origin` points to the task repository). No linked GitHub issue or label catalog was supplied, so no labels are suggested.

## Evidence
- `sm-core/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/core/business/services/order/OrderServiceImpl.java:117-215` processes orders and decrements inventory, but looks up a product with `productService.getById(orderProduct.getId())` (the order-product ID), logs inventory mismatches instead of rejecting, and decrements after creating the order.
- `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/store/controller/order/facade/OrderFacadeImpl.java:1196-1330` builds order products from the cart and delegates to `OrderServiceImpl`; checkout therefore shares the defective inventory path for both API forms.
- `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/store/controller/order/facade/OrderFacadeImpl.java:1625-1653` makes status changes idempotent only by returning on the same status; it does not restore inventory or prevent transitions out of CANCELED.
- `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/store/api/v1/order/OrderApi.java:494-518` exposes the required private status endpoint.
- `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/store/controller/shoppingCart/facade/ShoppingCartFacadeImpl.java:130-190` adds cart items without checking requested quantity against stock; duplicate additions increment quantity without a bound check.
- `ShoppingCartFacadeImpl.java:260-330` rejects zero stock when adding, but does not compare a positive requested quantity to available stock.
- `ShoppingCartFacadeImpl.java:570-680` updates one or many cart entries directly and saves them; multi-update mutates entries before persistence and has no all-or-nothing stock validation. Existing zero-quantity behavior is used for removal in the API tests.
- `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/store/api/v1/shoppingCart/ShoppingCartApi.java:65-110,149-170` exposes POST cart creation, PUT single-item modification, and POST `/multi`; wrappers currently convert ordinary failures to `ServiceRuntimeException`.
- `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/populator/catalog/ReadableProductPopulator.java:493-504` maps `ProductAvailability.productQuantity` to the product `quantity` and sets `canBePurchased` only when quantity is positive and the merchant product is available.
- `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/mapper/catalog/product/ReadableProductMapper.java:350-365` contains the parallel product mapping path and must receive the same zero-stock semantics.
- `sm-core/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/core/model/catalog/product/availability/ProductAvailability.java:80-105` defines the persisted quantity as `productQuantity`, the inventory source represented by the v2 product quantity.
- `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/store/api/exception/RestErrorHandler.java:43-57` currently maps `ServiceRuntimeException` to HTTP 400; a dedicated 409 exception/handler or equivalent propagation is needed.
- Existing coverage is primarily in `sm-shop/src/test/java/com/salesmanager/test/shop/integration/cart/ShoppingCartAPIIntegrationTest.java` and `OrderApiIntegrationTest.java`; no tests were found covering atomic stock reservation, cancellation restoration, or zero-stock v2 flags.

## Problem and implementation scope
Implement a single inventory policy around the availability record that supplies the v2 product `quantity`. Validate all cart additions and quantity increases before mutating or saving the cart. For multi-update, validate the complete proposed cart state first, then apply all changes. Validate the complete cart before payment/order creation; reject insufficient stock with 409 and leave both cart and inventory unchanged. Decrement the SKU/product actually represented by each order line exactly once, atomically with order creation and inventory updates. Add cancellation restoration keyed to the persisted order product’s underlying product/availability, mark restoration as already applied (using durable order state/history or an equivalent invariant), reject transitions from CANCELED to another status with 409, and leave other status changes inventory-neutral. Ensure both v2 product mapping paths calculate `available=false` and `canBePurchased=false` at zero quantity while preserving merchant-disabled availability.

## Acceptance checks
1. Anonymous and authenticated checkout with multiple distinct SKUs decrements only each matching SKU by its ordered quantity.
2. Any insufficient line returns HTTP 409; no order, payment-side inventory mutation, or cart mutation is observable.
3. POST cart creation, PUT cart modification, and POST `/multi` reject quantities above stock with 409; failed multi-updates leave every original line unchanged. Decreases/removals remain allowed, including zero removal semantics.
4. CANCELED restores every ordered quantity exactly once; repeating CANCELED is a no-op; any later non-CANCELED status returns 409 without changing stock; non-cancel status changes do not affect stock.
5. v2 GET product quantity reaches zero with `available=false` and `canBePurchased=false`, returns to true after restoration/replenishment, and remains unavailable when the merchant flag is false.
6. Add integration/unit tests for the above paths, including distinct-product regression coverage and rollback/atomicity assertions. Run the relevant Maven module tests and the full build if practical.

## Likely affected components and complexity
Likely changes span `sm-core` order/inventory services, `sm-shop` order and cart facades/APIs, REST exception handling, both product mappers/populators, and integration tests. The work is high complexity because it requires consistent SKU-to-inventory identity, transaction boundaries/rollback behavior, durable idempotency for cancellation, and preserving existing cart removal semantics. Requirements are sufficiently explicit for direct implementation; no separate design approval is required.

This applies to creating a cart (POST /api/v1/cart/), changing one product's quantity (PUT /api/v1/cart/{code}) and changing several at once (POST /api/v1/cart/{code}/multi, where either every change is made or none is). A product with no stock can't be added at all (HTTP 409). Lowering a quantity or removing a product is always allowed.
- Setting an order's status to CANCELED (PUT /api/v1/private/orders/{id}/status) puts each ordered product's quantity back into its stock. This happens once: setting CANCELED again on an order that is already canceled changes nothing. A canceled order can't be given any other status (HTTP 409 Conflict, and stock is unchanged). Other status changes don't change stock.
- GET /api/v2/product/{sku} shows "available": false and "canBePurchased": false for a product with no stock, and shows it as available again once it has stock. A product the merchant marked unavailable stays unavailable whatever its stock.
